newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel says Clinton criticism expected - Itim.
newsitem.headline: Israel says Clinton criticism expected - Itim.

text.p: Israel said on Monday that U.S. President Bill Clinton's criticism of its decision to build a new Jewish neighbourhood in Arab East Jerusalem was expected, Israel's Itim news agency said.
"The United States always opposed Israel's policy in Jerusalem and that did not interfere with Israel building in it in the past," Itim quoted a government source as saying.
"The government sources added that the government of Israel intended to implement its building projects throughout the city," Itim added.

Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's spokesman Shai Bazak refused to comment when asked by Reuters about Clinton's criticism on Monday of Israel's approval last week of a plan that will build 6,500 homes for Jews in Arab East Jerusalem.

"I would have preferred the decision not have been made because I don't think it builds confidence. I think it builds mistrust," Clinton said at the start of a White House meeting with Palestinian President Yasser Arafat.

Israel captured East Jerusalem along with the West Bank and the Gaza Strip in the 1967 Middle East war. In a move not recognised internationally, it later annexed East Jerusalem, declaring it part of an indivisible capital. Palestinians want East Jerusalem to be the capital of a future state.
Palestinians view Israeli building in East Jerusalem as preempting negotiations on the city's status that are to be part of final peace talks set to resume in the next several weeks.
